Requirement: For every committed ledger transaction, total debits equal total credits.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given balanced and unbalanced generated entry sets; when building and committing; then only equal debit/credit totals commit and the unbalanced set leaves zero rows.

Requirement: Money uses integer minor units; double and float are prohibited.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given API/constructor inputs including decimal floating values and integer minor units; when money is created/persisted; then only integer minor units are accepted and code/static checks find no double/float money fields.

Requirement: Every amount has an ISO currency, and every ledger account has one configured currency.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given an entry without currency or an account with a different currency; when posting; then validation rejects before commit; matching ISO currency commits.

Requirement: Ledger transactions and entries are immutable after commit.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given a committed transaction; when application and runtime DB role attempt update/delete; then APIs expose no mutation and database grants/triggers reject with unchanged rows.

Requirement: Corrections are new reversal or adjustment transactions, never edits.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given an incorrect committed posting; when correction is requested; then a linked reversal/adjustment is appended and original rows/checksum remain unchanged.

Requirement: A transaction and all entries commit atomically.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given injected failure after transaction header and before final entry/outbox; when transaction rolls back; then header, entries, snapshot change, and outbox are all absent.

Requirement: A failed posting creates no partial transaction or entry set.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given posting policy/constraint failure at each write step; when posting aborts; then no partial transaction or entry set is queryable.

Requirement: One source financial event maps to at most one effective ledger transaction.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given two concurrent commands for the same source type/ID; when both post; then one transaction commits and the other returns the original/conflict without second effect.

Requirement: A posting idempotency key reused with different canonical entries is rejected.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given a completed posting key; when reused with identical canonical entries then original returns; when one amount/account changes then POSTING_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and no rows commit.

Requirement: All accounts in a transaction use the transaction currency.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given USD transaction with one EUR account; when posting; then currency mismatch rejects; all-USD accounts pass.

Requirement: Every transaction has at least two entries and at least one debit and one credit.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given zero/one-entry, all-debit, all-credit, and valid two-sided sets; when building transaction; then only at least two entries with both directions pass.

Requirement: Entry amount is strictly positive; direction carries debit or credit meaning.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given zero, negative, and positive entry amounts; when creating entries; then only positive magnitude with explicit direction is accepted.

Requirement: Checked arithmetic detects overflow before commit.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given values near Long maximum and configured business limit; when fee/total arithmetic occurs; then Math exact overflow/limit exception occurs before persistence.

Requirement: Account locks are acquired in deterministic account-ID order for balance-affecting writes.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given two concurrent postings referencing accounts in opposite input order; when locks are acquired; then SQL order is sorted UUID and both complete or bounded-retry without cyclic deadlock.

Requirement: A reversal references exactly one original transaction and cannot reverse more than the un-reversed effective amount.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given original amount 100 and prior reversal 40; when reversing 60 then pass; reversing 61 or a second full reversal fails.

Requirement: A transaction cannot reverse itself or form a reversal cycle.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given self-reference and A->B->A reversal attempts; when validating graph; then both reject and no cycle commits.

Requirement: Balance snapshots are derived views; immutable entries remain authoritative.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given entries totaling 100 and a deliberately stale snapshot 80; when authoritative balance is rebuilt; then entry log returns 100 and snapshot can be repaired.

Requirement: A stale snapshot can affect read latency but cannot authorize an invalid write.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given stale snapshot suggesting funds available but entry-derived balance does not; when balance-affecting write is authorized; then write rejects using authoritative locked data.

Requirement: Every posting records source type, source ID, correlation ID, and posting policy version.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given posting missing source/correlation/policy fields; when posting; then reject; valid posting persists all fields and timeline can link them.

Requirement: Database permissions deny application-level update and delete of committed ledger entries.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given runtime and migration database roles; when each attempts update/delete on committed ledger rows; then runtime access fails, controlled schema migration remains separate/audited, and original rows remain unchanged.

Requirement: A ledger imbalance attempt is rejected, logged without sensitive payloads, and increments a domain alarm metric.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given unbalanced input containing canary sensitive text; when rejected; then metric increments, sanitized error/log contains IDs only, and canary text is absent.

Requirement: Currency minor-unit rules are validated at boundaries; seed examples use USD but the domain remains currency-aware.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given USD, JPY, and three-decimal currency boundary inputs; when converted; then supported exponent rules accept exact minor units and reject excess fractional precision.

Requirement: Every payment belongs to exactly one merchant.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given merchant A and B; when A creates and B reads/commands A payment; then B gets RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN-equivalent and ownership remains A.

Requirement: A payment’s amount and currency are positive, valid, and immutable after authorization begins.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given a CREATED payment and the same payment after authorization begins; when amount or currency mutation is requested; then only the explicitly allowed pre-authorization command may pass and every later mutation is rejected with stored values unchanged.

Requirement: Only transitions listed in the payment state-machine specification are allowed.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given every state/command pair; when transition table is exercised; then listed transitions pass and all unlisted pairs return PAYMENT_INVALID_STATE.

Requirement: Total captured amount never exceeds total successfully authorized amount.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given authorization 100 with captured 60 and concurrent capture requests of 40, 41, 30, and 30; when the requests execute; then cumulative capture never exceeds 100 and only a valid version/idempotent winner commits.

Requirement: Total refunded amount never exceeds total effectively captured amount.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given captured amount 100 and prior refund 60 with refund requests of 40, 41, and concurrent over-refunds; when they execute; then only valid cumulative refunds commit and refunded total never exceeds 100.

Requirement: A timeout or connection loss is not automatically classified as provider failure.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given provider executes then connection drops; when adapter classifies ambiguity; then payment is not marked failed and query/reconciliation path is created.

Requirement: Ambiguous provider execution produces an explicit *_UNKNOWN state.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given ambiguous authorize/capture/cancel/refund outcomes; when processed; then corresponding UNKNOWN state and operation snapshot are stored.

Requirement: One provider operation key maps to at most one effective external operation.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given repeated/concurrent calls with one provider operation key; when simulator processes; then one effective operation exists and all responses reference it.

Requirement: The same idempotency key and semantic request return the original result or current in-progress result.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same merchant/operation/key and same canonical hash sequentially/concurrently; when requested; then original or IN_PROGRESS result returns with one operation ID.

Requirement: The same idempotency key with a different semantic request is rejected.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same scoped key with changed amount/currency/reference; when requested; then 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and no second command begins.

Requirement: Idempotency scope includes merchant, operation type, and key; keys do not collide across merchants.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given identical key used by two merchants and two operation types; when requested; then each valid scope is independent while duplicates inside one scope converge.

Requirement: Provider callbacks are deduplicated by provider and provider event ID.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same signed callback event ID delivered three times; when processed; then one provider-event row and one effective transition occur.

Requirement: An older or out-of-order provider event cannot regress a terminal or more authoritative state.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given success evidence followed by older rejection; when both arrive; then state remains successful and older event is timeline evidence only.

Requirement: A capture cannot start while another capture for the same remaining authorization is in progress or unknown unless policy proves it is safe.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given capture IN_PROGRESS or CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; when another capture starts; then guard rejects before provider call; after confirmed non-execution valid capture can start.

Requirement: Cancellation cannot be confirmed while a capture outcome is unknown.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; when cancel command arrives; then it rejects and no cancellation operation is created.

Requirement: Every external attempt records operation key, attempt number, request time, deadline, result classification, and sanitized provider reference.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given success, rejection, timeout, and pre-execution failure; when attempts persist; then each contains key, number, request/deadline, result class, and sanitized reference.

Requirement: Merchant-supplied state, provider, fee, account, and internal reference fields are ignored or rejected.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given request body supplies state/provider/fee/account/internal IDs; when validated; then FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED and server-derived fields remain authoritative.

Requirement: A payment timeline is append-only from the product perspective; corrections append new evidence.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given later correction/evidence; when timeline queried; then original items remain byte-identical and new item is appended in stable order.

Requirement: Each successful capture has one source financial event ID used for ledger-posting idempotency.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given one successful capture; when local transaction commits/retries; then one source financial event ID links exactly one ledger posting.

Requirement: Unknown outcomes are resolved only through authoritative provider query, signed callback, statement evidence, or an explicitly audited manual process.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given timeout with no authoritative evidence; when automatic/manual failure is attempted; then reject; signed query/callback/statement or audited manual evidence can resolve.

Requirement: An ambiguous cancellation enters CANCELLATION_UNKNOWN; capture and duplicate cancellation remain blocked until authoritative resolution.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given cancellation response lost; when ambiguity stored; then CANCELLATION_UNKNOWN blocks capture/second cancel until original key resolves.

Requirement: Every *_UNKNOWN state stores the exact pre-operation state and amounts so confirmed non-execution restores deterministically.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given each UNKNOWN entered from different state/amounts; when non-execution confirmed; then exact stored pre-state/amounts/authorizationClosed are restored.

Requirement: Every imported statement has a source identity, checksum, import time, schema version, and immutable raw-object reference.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given statement import; when accepted; then source ID, checksum, import time, schema version, immutable object reference persist; missing fields reject.

Requirement: The same statement or row cannot create duplicate effective reconciliation evidence.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given duplicate file and duplicate row delivered; when importing/matching; then one effective evidence row/classification exists.

Requirement: Matching is deterministic for a recorded rules version.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same evidence and rules version on repeat runs; when matching; then identical classifications/checksum result.

Requirement: Exact matches, tolerated differences, duplicates, missing internal records, and missing external records are distinct outcomes.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given fixtures for exact, tolerated, duplicate, missing-internal, and missing-external; when matched; then each distinct outcome is preserved.

Requirement: A difference is never silently discarded.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given unmatched row; when run completes; then queryable exception exists; no code path discards it.

Requirement: Every exception remains queryable after resolution.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given resolved exception; when historical/open/all queries run; then exception and resolution remain queryable.

Requirement: Resolution appends a resolution action; it does not delete or rewrite original evidence.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given resolution action; when committed; then raw/import/match evidence unchanged and new append-only action links it.

Requirement: Manual resolution records principal, reason, evidence, timestamp, and before/after classification.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given manual resolution missing actor/reason/evidence/before-after; when submitted; then reject; complete action audits all fields.

Requirement: Reconciliation may resolve an unknown payment operation but cannot bypass payment and ledger invariants.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given reconciliation confirms capture success; when resolving payment; then state/amount guards and ledger posting idempotency still apply.

Requirement: If provider evidence confirms success, the corresponding financial posting remains idempotent.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given repeated success evidence for one operation; when posting repair runs; then one source event/ledger transaction exists.

Requirement: If provider evidence confirms non-execution, the system may return to a safe retryable state only through an explicit transition.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given evidence proves non-execution; when retryable transition runs; then only explicit state-machine restoration occurs with original snapshot.

Requirement: File parsing is bounded by file size, row count, column count, field length, and processing time.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given file/row/column/field/time limits exceeded; when import runs; then bounded failure/checkpoint and no resource exhaustion.

Requirement: CSV exports neutralize spreadsheet formula injection.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given export cells beginning =,+,-,@ and tabs; when CSV generated; then neutralized values cannot execute spreadsheet formulas.

Requirement: Amount comparison uses currency-aware integer minor units and recorded rounding policy.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given multi-currency amounts and boundary rounding; when compared; then integer minor-unit and recorded policy produce deterministic classification.

Requirement: Reconciliation runs are restartable from persisted checkpoints without duplicating matches or resolutions.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given matcher killed after checkpoint; when restarted; then remaining rows process without duplicate match/resolution actions.

Requirement: No state-changing operation executes without an authenticated principal or service identity.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given unauthenticated user and missing service identity; when state-changing endpoints/workers execute; then deny before domain/repository/provider action.

Requirement: Merchant authorization is derived from the authenticated principal, never trusted from request body ownership fields.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given body merchantId differs from authenticated merchant; when command runs; then body ownership is rejected/ignored and no cross-merchant row is touched.

Requirement: A merchant can access only its own payments, settlements, webhook configuration, and permitted ledger views.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given merchant A IDs guessed by merchant B across payment/settlement/webhook/ledger views; when queried; then safe not-found/forbidden response and no existence leak.

Requirement: Provider callbacks are processed only after signature, timestamp, and replay-window validation.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given invalid signature, stale timestamp, replayed valid event, and valid fresh event; when callback arrives; then first three reject/dedupe and only valid fresh event applies.

Requirement: Raw card numbers, CVV, bank credentials, and real payment credentials are not accepted or stored.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given requests/files containing PAN-like, CVV, bank credential, or real provider secret fields; when validated; then reject and persistence/telemetry scan finds none.

Requirement: Provider and signing secrets never appear in logs, traces, exceptions, API responses, or audit payloads.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given canary provider/signing secrets and forced errors; when logs/traces/API/audit are scanned; then canaries are absent.

Requirement: User-controlled internal state, provider choice, fee, ledger account, and settlement fields are rejected or ignored.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given internal provider/fee/account/settlement fields; when API binds; then FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED and domain uses policy/server values.

Requirement: Every privileged action records actor, role, action, target, reason where required, correlation ID, and timestamp.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given privileged resolution/reversal/replay/rotation; when executed; then audit contains actor, role, action, target, required reason, correlation, timestamp, outcome.

Requirement: Audit records are append-only through the application.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given committed audit event; when runtime update/delete attempted; then DB rejects and original event remains.

Requirement: Idempotency cannot be bypassed through alternate routes, aliases, or API versions for the same operation.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same semantic capture through path alias/version; when same business idempotency scope used; then one operation/effect exists.

Requirement: Request bodies, headers, files, list filters, and pagination have explicit size and rate limits.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given over-limit body/header/file/filter/page/rate requests; when received; then bounded 400/413/429 response occurs before expensive processing.

Requirement: Errors reveal stable public codes but not stack traces, SQL, secrets, internal topology, or cross-tenant existence.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given SQL/stack/secret/cross-tenant errors; when returned; then stable public code/correlation only, with sensitive internals absent.

Requirement: Outbound merchant webhook URLs are validated against SSRF policy before activation and before delivery.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given localhost, metadata IP, private DNS rebinding, disallowed scheme, and allowed HTTPS endpoint; when activating/delivering later; then unsafe targets reject at both checks.

Requirement: Dependency and container vulnerabilities are scanned in CI with defined severity gates.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given vulnerable dependency/container fixtures at severity gate; when CI scan runs; then build blocks per policy and accepted exception requires expiry/owner.

Requirement: Database roles enforce least privilege by module and deny mutation of immutable ledger history.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given module DB roles; when each accesses another schema or mutates immutable ledger; then least-privilege grants reject while approved operations pass.

Requirement: Service-to-service identities are distinct from user identities and have narrow permissions.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given user JWT presented to service-only endpoint and service token to interactive endpoint; when authenticated; then audience/type checks reject both misuse cases.

Requirement: Replay, reconciliation, reversal, and secret-rotation operations require elevated permissions.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given ordinary merchant/ops role attempts replay/reconcile/reverse/rotate; when authorized; then deny; elevated scoped role with reason passes and audits.

Requirement: Authentication or authorization failure is fail-closed; unavailable policy storage never grants access.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given identity/policy verification unavailable or invalid; when request arrives; then fail closed and no cached permissive fallback grants access.

Requirement: Sensitive fields have explicit telemetry redaction tests.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given each sensitive-field canary through success/failure paths; when telemetry exported; then automated scan finds zero occurrences.

Requirement: Security controls have integration tests, not only configuration review.
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given security configuration appears correct; when integration suite attacks tenant, signature, limits, SSRF policy, and DB roles; then controls are proven at runtime.

Requirement: Each settlement batch belongs to one merchant, currency, policy version, and settlement cycle.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given batch creation with mixed merchant/currency/policy/cycle items; when calculated; then reject; homogeneous batch persists immutable ownership fields.

Requirement: A source payment item is included at most once in an effective settlement batch.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same payment item selected by concurrent workers; when batches commit; then uniqueness allows one effective inclusion.

Requirement: Batch calculation uses a fixed cut-off instant and records the time zone and policy version.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given cutoff around timezone/DST boundary; when calculating; then fixed instant/timezone/policy select deterministic items.

Requirement: Configuration changes after calculation do not silently change an existing batch.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given policy changes after READY; when batch queried/recalculated; then existing totals/version remain and new cycle uses new policy.

Requirement: Batch totals equal the sum of immutable included items and adjustments.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given immutable items/adjustments; when totals persisted; then recomputation equals gross/fees/refunds/reserves/adjustments/net; mismatch rejects.

Requirement: A payout instruction has a deterministic idempotency key.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given same merchant/cycle/batch submitted twice; when payout key generated; then exact same deterministic key and one instruction.

Requirement: A provider payout timeout becomes PAYOUT_UNKNOWN, not immediate failure.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given provider payout succeeds and response drops; when handled; then PAYOUT_UNKNOWN and no second instruction.

Requirement: A restarted worker resumes from persisted batch state and checkpoint.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given worker killed after checkpoint; when restarted; then resumes next item/state using same batch/key without duplicate inclusion.

Requirement: One merchant’s failure does not block calculation or submission for unrelated merchants.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given merchant A batch fails and B is ready; when workers run; then B progresses independently.

Requirement: Negative payable balances follow an explicit carry-forward or reserve policy; they are never silently paid.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given negative payable; when settlement calculates; then configured carry-forward/receivable/reserve path applies and payout is not silently negative.

Requirement: Refunds or disputes after inclusion create later adjustments; they do not mutate the closed batch.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given refund/dispute after confirmed batch; when processed; then closed batch unchanged and later adjustment item created.

Requirement: A batch cannot move to CONFIRMED without authoritative payout evidence.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given submitted payout without authoritative evidence; when confirm attempted; then reject; query/callback/statement success permits CONFIRMED.

Requirement: Manual batch resolution requires privilege, reason, evidence, and audit.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given manual batch resolution with missing privilege/reason/evidence; when attempted; then reject; complete approved action appends audit.

Requirement: Every batch exposes gross, fees, refunds, reserves, adjustments, and net payout as independently explainable values.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given a batch; when API/export queried; then gross, fees, refunds, reserves, adjustments, and net independently sum and link to items.

Requirement: Settlement calculation is repeatable from its recorded inputs and policy version.
Test Layer: Domain + PostgreSQL concurrency + payout failure injection
Concrete Given/When/Then Scenario: Given recorded inputs/policy/checkpoint; when calculation reruns; then identical item set/totals/checksum result.
